context:
Goal: the record on lane lint states what lane lint runs.
Problem (rule): decision lanes-run-no-full-ci-job says lane lint runs only the fast lint steps and no hook suite or mutation test. In fact bin/ci-job runs every `python3 lint/*.py` step, the Stop-hook guard suite included, and its own cost line says 550-660 s. A record you ruled on changes only on your word.
Based on (measured): `merge --lane-lint 1988` ran about 55 fixture suites and passed the 600 s command cap (lane windows-local-lint and its round-1 reviewer, 2026-11-08).
Departs from: main, where the record says lane lint is fast and runs no hook suite — it says lane lint runs every lint CI step, fixture suites included, and drops "fast".
Meanwhile: the lane goes on with #1988; making lane lint fast again stays with step lane-lint-cloud-time-limit.

options.gain: The record is true, so a lane reading it plans for a slow lint run.
options.how: Line 5 is rewritten in place to say what bin/ci-job runs; speed stays with step lane-lint-cloud-time-limit.
options.label: Rewrite the line to match
options.lose: The record no longer states that lane lint should be fast; that aim lives only in the step until it lands.

options.how: The line stays; it becomes true again when step lane-lint-cloud-time-limit lands.
options.label: Keep the text until lint is fast
options.lose: The record is false meanwhile, and lanes plan for a fast run that hits the 600 s cap.

ref: decision lanes-run-no-full-ci-job (line 5); bin/ci-job:200 and :248; checks.yml:234-235; step lane-lint-cloud-time-limit
reply: Withdrawn 07:39 CST Nov 8: your ruling on page item 27 a (2026-10-27) already answers it. Lane lint runs only the fast steps and no hook suite, so the tool goes back to the ruling and the record stays. Home: step lane-lint-cloud-time-limit.
short: Lane lint record: say what it really runs
title: May the lanes-run-no-full-ci-job record be rewritten to say lane lint runs every lint CI step, fixture suites included?
